scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is past the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Sofía Martinez and I'm 65. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Sofía, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and my email is sofia.m@email.com.

Thank you, Sofía. I have successfully verified your account. I can see the transaction from 34 days ago. While our 'Service Terms and Conditions, Section 4.2' state that refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the billing date, I can see that this is your first time requesting an exception.
That's correct, I've been a loyal customer for years and I've never had an issue before. I really hope you can help me out.

I appreciate your long-standing loyalty, Sofía. Given your history with us, I am authorized to override the 30-day window as a one-time courtesy. I have processed the full refund of $49.99 to your original payment method. You should see the credit appear in your bank account within 3-5 business days.
Oh, that is such a relief! Thank you so much for your help today.
You are very welcome, Sofía. I'm glad we could get that resolved for you. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and applied a one-time policy exception for a loyal customer to refund a charge outside the 30-day window.

judge_scores.justification: The agent handled the situation exceptionally well by balancing policy compliance with personalized empathy. They correctly identified the account, cited specific policy (Section 4.2), and used their authority to grant a valid loyalty exception without unnecessary friction or escalation.
